title: FDA and EU GMP Expectations for Cloud-Hosted and SaaS Computerized Systems
summary: FDA and EU GMP expectations for cloud and SaaS computerized systems: Annex 11, supplier qualification, data integrity and related 483 and warning-letter precedents.
body_markdown:
## Cloud-hosted and SaaS GMP computerized systems: what FDA and EU regulators expect


Moving a GMP computerized system to the cloud, or buying it as software as a service (SaaS), changes who runs the infrastructure. It does not change who is accountable. FDA guidance, EU GMP Annex 11, the draft revised Annex 11, PIC/S and MHRA guidance all start from the same point: the regulated company keeps responsibility for validation, data integrity and record availability, and must show inspectors evidence that it has assessed, contracted with and overseen its provider. Enforcement records show that inspectors mostly cite the basics: unqualified software suppliers, reliance on vendor validation without the firm's own review, unvalidated quality-system software, and weak access, audit trail and backup controls.


### The common principle: accountability stays with the regulated user


- **FDA (drugs):** A quality agreement cannot transfer statutory or regulatory CGMP responsibilities. The owner's quality unit remains responsible for approving or rejecting a contractor's product or service[180](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=180)[181](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=181) .
- **FDA (clinical records, Part 11):** Regulated entities may contract for data hosting and cloud computing but remain responsible for ensuring their electronic records meet applicable Part 11 requirements[213](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=213) .
- **EU (draft revised Annex 11, July 2025):** Outsourcing does not transfer GMP responsibility. The regulated user remains fully responsible for compliance, for retaining supporting evidence and for providing it for regulatory review (clause 2.6)[119](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=119)[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=523) .
- **PIC/S PI 041-1:** Computerised-system principles apply equally when provision is outsourced. The regulated entity remains responsible for managing and assessing the service against GMP/GDP requirements. Its pharmaceutical quality system should address vendor management, IT security, and decentralised or cloud-based storage, processing, transfer and retrieval of records[107](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=107)[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=108) .


### FDA expectations


#### Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP (Q&A)


The drug CGMP data integrity Q&A does not address cloud hosting by name. It does set the controls a hosted system must still deliver:


- **Workflow validation (Q3):** Each CGMP workflow is an intended use and should be validated. The extent of validation should match the system's risk. Qualifying a platform alone does not show that a particular workflow's steps and calculations work correctly[149](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=149) . For SaaS, this means a vendor's platform qualification does not replace validation of the configured workflows the firm actually uses.
- **Audit trail review (Q7 to Q8):** Personnel reviewing a CGMP record should review the audit trails for changes to that record's data. Production and control records, including audit trails, must be reviewed and approved by the quality unit. Review frequency follows the regulation where one is specified; otherwise it is set by risk assessment[150](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=150) .
- **Access controls (Q4 to Q5):** Only authorized personnel may change computerized CGMP records. FDA recommends technical restrictions, a system administrator independent of those responsible for record content, and documented access privileges. Shared credentials cannot attribute actions to an individual[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=151) .
- **Backup (Q1(e)):** A backup is a securely maintained true copy, exact and complete, protected against alteration, erasure or loss, including metadata, for the full retention period. A temporary crash-recovery copy does not meet this requirement[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=152) .
- **Retention and CGMP records (Q1(b), Q12):** Data must be retained with all metadata needed to reconstruct the CGMP activity[153](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=153) . All data generated to satisfy a CGMP requirement become CGMP records[154](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=154) .


#### Computer Software Assurance (final, February 2026)


*Computer Software Assurance for Production and Quality Management System Software* is final, dated February 3, 2026, and nonbinding[360](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=360) . It is FDA's most explicit treatment of SaaS and cloud-hosted software for production and quality system use:


- **Scope:** The intended-use determination asks whether software is used directly in, or supports, production or the quality management system. The validation requirement includes relevant IaaS, PaaS and SaaS uses[384](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=384)[385](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=385)[386](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=386)[387](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=387) . The guidance defines SaaS as use of a provider's cloud-hosted applications, generally without control of the underlying infrastructure[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=220) .
- **Leveraging suppliers:** Manufacturers can leverage validation work by suppliers and cloud service providers while maintaining a validated state[219](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=219) . Vendor development practices, validation work and electronic information can be a starting point, after which the manufacturer decides what additional assurance is needed[389](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=389)[390](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=390) .
- **Vendor evaluation:** Evaluation of cloud-based, on-premise or hybrid vendors should be risk-based, recognizing that an onsite audit may not be feasible. Documentation and certifications can support the evaluation[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=223)[391](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=391) .
- **SaaS worked example (PLM system, Example 4):** The manufacturer assesses the vendor's development practices, quality system, cybersecurity and infrastructure availability, documents that evaluation, and establishes a service agreement covering security, data integrity, privacy, availability, change management and business continuity. For automatic vendor updates, it reviews the vendor's change and test documentation, assesses the impact on intended use, and performs risk-based assurance testing[221](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=221) . Assurance activities in the example include configuration verification and exploratory user acceptance testing[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=222) .
- **Data integrity controls to check:** retention, complete copies, time-stamped audit trails and access controls[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=224) .


#### Part 11 and IT service providers (clinical investigations Q&A, October 2024)


The final *Electronic Systems, Electronic Records, and Electronic Signatures in Clinical Investigations: Questions and Answers* (October 1, 2024) is written for clinical investigations[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=191) . It is still the clearest FDA statement of what a contract with a hosting or cloud provider should contain, and GMP teams often use it as a benchmark:


- **Provider selection:** Consider the provider's oversight policies, validation procedures for the services used, ability to provide complete copies and access throughout retention, migration, backup and recovery procedures, access controls, time-stamped audit trails, and protection of data at rest and in transit[213](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=213) .
- **Written agreement (Q17):** The agreement should address data integrity and security safeguards, scope of work, each party's roles and quality management responsibilities, and a plan for access to data throughout the retention period. Obligations not specifically and lawfully transferred stay with the sponsor[306](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=306) .
- **Validation evidence on inspection:** If validation is done by or for the sponsor, the regulated entity must provide the requested validation documentation, including documentation held by the provider[308](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=308) . Agreements and evidence of oversight should be available to FDA on request (Q18)[309](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=309) .
- **FDA access to providers (Q19):** FDA may inspect providers that have assumed regulatory responsibilities, and may run focused inspections where data integrity is in question[310](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=310)[218](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=218) .
- **Exit:** Cloud-stored records and metadata must be preserved and available for inspection. When a hosted-system contract ends, sponsors should obtain and retain the metadata linked to the corresponding data[214](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=214)[217](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=217) .


#### Quality agreements for contracted CGMP services


FDA's *Contract Manufacturing Arrangements for Drugs: Quality Agreements* (November 2016)[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=159) expects the agreement to assign document creation, review, approval and retention roles, to explain how original records or true copies will be readily available for inspection, and to provide for CGMP-compliant electronic storage and immediate retrieval during retention[182](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=182) . It should allow owner audits, set expectations for FDA inspections, and address communication of inspection findings[187](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=187)[188](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=188) .


### EU expectations


#### Current EU GMP Annex 11 (Computerised Systems)


The Annex 11 text in EudraLex Volume 4 is listed with a date of 20 December 2010[497](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=497) . It does not use the words "cloud" or "SaaS", but its supplier and data clauses apply directly to hosted systems[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=25) :


Clause Expectation relevant to hosted and SaaS systems


Principle, 1 Validate the application and qualify the IT infrastructure. Use documented risk assessment to set the extent of validation and data integrity controls[26](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=26)[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=27) .


3.1 Formal agreements must state the responsibilities of third parties that provide, install, configure, integrate, validate, maintain, modify or retain a system or service, or process data. IT departments are treated in the same way[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=25) .


3.2 Supplier competence and reliability are selection factors. The need for an audit is based on risk assessment[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=25) .


3.3 Documentation supplied with commercial off-the-shelf products should be reviewed against user requirements[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=25) .


3.4 Supplier or developer quality system and audit information should be available to inspectors on request[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=25) .


4.5 to 4.6 Assess the supplier and take reasonable steps to ensure appropriate development quality management. Formally assess bespoke or customised systems across the life cycle[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=28)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=29) .


4.8 Check that migrated data retain their value and meaning[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=29) .


7.1 to 7.2 Protect stored data, ensure access throughout retention, back up regularly, and check backup integrity and restorability during validation and periodically[30](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=30) .


9 Risk-based audit trails of GMP-relevant changes and deletions, with reasons documented, available, intelligible and regularly reviewed[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=31) .


12 Restrict access to authorised persons. Record creation, change and cancellation of access rights[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=32) .


16 Business continuity arrangements for systems that support critical processes, documented and tested[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=33) .


17 Archived data checked for accessibility, readability and integrity, including when system changes are planned[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=34) .


#### EU GMP Chapter 7 (Outsourced Activities)


A hosted GMP system is an outsourced activity. Chapter 7 requires the contract giver to assess the contract acceptor's legality, suitability and competence (7.5) and to control and review outsourced activities through its quality system (7.4)[458](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=458) . A written contract must define responsibilities and communication processes (7.14)[459](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=459)[460](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=460) , permit audits of the contract acceptor and agreed subcontractors (7.17)[461](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=461) , and keep records of outsourced activities available to the contract giver (7.16)[462](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=462) .


#### Draft revised Annex 11 and Chapter 4 (July 2025)


The draft revised Annex 11 and draft revised Chapter 4 are both dated 7 July 2025 and remain drafts[463](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=463)[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=523)[96](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=96) . They follow a 2022 concept paper[464](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=464) , which proposed that users of critical provider-validated or provider-operated systems, including cloud services, have complete validation and operational documentation available at inspection, potentially with provider help[120](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=120) . The draft text addresses hosted services directly:


- **As-a-service systems (6.1, 6.3, 6.4):** GMP requirements apply whether a system is provided as a service. A SaaS vendor may supply the requirements specification, but the regulated user should review, approve, take ownership of and control it for the implemented version. Requirements should stay accurate as the system changes and form the basis of qualification and validation[529](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=529)[530](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=530)[531](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=531) .
- **Supplier audit or assessment (7.2):** Before relying on a vendor's or provider's qualification or operation, the regulated user should audit or thoroughly assess its procedures and documentation, scaled to risk and system criticality, and then decide what work can be leveraged[527](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=527)[528](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=528) .
- **SLAs, KPIs and contract content (73, 75):** The regulated user should oversee provider performance against agreed SLAs and KPIs. Contracts, or approved procedures for internal IT, should cover activities and documentation, applicable procedures and regulations, reporting and oversight, response and resolution times, audit conditions, and support during regulatory inspections[532](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=532)[533](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=533)[535](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=535) .
- **Inspector access:** Qualification and operation documentation should be accessible and explainable from the regulated user's facility, with provider support if needed[534](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=534) .
- **Security (15.1, 2.7):** The regulated user should maintain an information security management system that safeguards authorised access and detects and prevents unauthorised access, and should respond to new threats in a timely way[536](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=536)[537](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=537) .
- **Hosted records (draft Chapter 4, 4.76):** Users of hosted services should understand, approve and justify the provider's controls on the basis of an SLA, and keep records available for human-readable review throughout retention[118](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=118) . Draft Chapter 4 also defines data ownership as assigning responsibility for data control to a process owner (4.15)[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=116)[117](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=117) .


The draft clauses reviewed do not say that a provider certification can replace the audit or assessment, and they do not set a cloud-specific exit or portability procedure beyond continued record availability and the general definition of migration[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=523)[538](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=538)[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=102)[118](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=118) . A companion draft Annex 22 on artificial intelligence carries the same date[469](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=469) .


#### Veterinary GMP: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2091


For veterinary medicinal products, Annex IV of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2091 (dated 17 October 2025) requires a written contract delineating responsibilities for outsourced computerised-system tasks, services or data processing, risk-based assessment of contractors including audits where appropriate, qualification of suppliers of software developed or adapted for manufacturing, and contractual access to their quality system information when inspectors ask for it[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=75) .


### PIC/S and MHRA


**PIC/S PI 041-1** expects supplier and service provider audits to verify data integrity measures, quality agreements that cover data governance, transparent reporting of errors and deviations, and notification of data integrity failures (10.3.2)[109](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=109)[110](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=110)[112](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=112) . External archiving providers should be assessed and archiving responsibilities written into a quality technical agreement, and contract acceptors should give reasonable access to data generated for the contract giver[109](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=109)[114](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=114) . Archive arrangements should preserve the software needed to review the data[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=115) .


**MHRA *Guidance on GxP data integrity*** (March 2018)[35](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=35) has a dedicated section, 6.20, on IT suppliers and service providers, including cloud providers and SaaS, PaaS and IaaS[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=66) . MHRA expects firms to:


- understand data ownership, retrieval, retention and security, and where data are physically held and which laws apply there[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=67) ;
- define responsibilities in a technical agreement, including timely access for the data owner and national competent authorities to data, metadata and audit trails, plus archiving and readability throughout retention[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=68) ;
- be able to restore the system to its validated state[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=69) ;
- include and test business continuity arrangements, and decide on a provider audit based on risk[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=70) .


Section 6.19 states that vendor-supplied validation data alone is not sufficient without considering the configured system and its intended use[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=71) .


### Enforcement precedents


#### Warning letters: supplier qualification and reliance on vendor validation


Except for Westwood (drug CGMP), these letters cite the device quality system regulation (21 CFR 820). They are device-sector analogs on software-supplier qualification and reliance on vendor validation, not cloud-hosting drug CGMP cases.


Company (letter date) Citation Finding


Westwood Laboratories LLC (Apr. 17, 2024) Drug CGMP FDA stated that the firm is responsible for validation of its HPLC system even though the vendor completed it on the firm's behalf. The validation documentation could not be located during the inspection[241](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/westwood-laboratories-llc-674728-04172024)[252](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/westwood-laboratories-llc-674728-04172024) .


Oertel Medical GmbH (June 11, 2012) 21 CFR 820.70(i), 820.50 No records showing the ERP system was validated for user needs and intended uses, gaps in control over vendor-installed updates, and no documentation that the software supplier was qualified or requalified[232](https://web.archive.org/web/20151003020406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2012/ucm309306.htm)[250](https://web.archive.org/web/20151003020406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2012/ucm309306.htm)[251](https://web.archive.org/web/20151003020406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2012/ucm309306.htm) .


Staar Surgical Co. (May 21, 2014) 21 CFR 820.50 A critical software supplier had been in pending status since 2007 and had never been audited or completed a supplier questionnaire[227](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423062156/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2014/ucm402449.htm)[249](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423062156/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2014/ucm402449.htm) .


F.P. Rubinstein Y Cia SRL (May 5, 2016) 21 CFR 820.70(i), 820.50 Complaint handling and data analysis software was not validated. Software development contractors were missing from the approved supplier list[226](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423061935/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2016/ucm515403.htm)[247](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423061935/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2016/ucm515403.htm)[248](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423061935/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2016/ucm515403.htm) .


Herniamesh S.r.l (Nov. 23, 2015) 21 CFR 820.70(i) Two systems for quality records, supplier evaluation, nonconformities, purchasing and production were not validated for quality-system use[492](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423060526/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2015/ucm503837.htm) .


Savaria Concord Lifts (Aug. 3, 2016); Bedfont Scientific (Feb. 4, 2016) 21 CFR 820.70(i) Software for design changes, complaints, CAPA, nonconformances and service was not validated for intended use[493](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423061923/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2016/ucm538430.htm)[494](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423061953/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2016/ucm515647.htm) .


Vitang Technology LLC (June 12, 2023) 21 CFR 820.70(i) A web application used to maintain complaint files was not validated for its intended use[496](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/vitang-technology-llc-653455-06122023) .


In a 2006 letter to Vapotherm, FDA described an off-the-shelf, web-based commercial complaint program used outside the firm's approved complaint procedure. The letter does not say where the program was hosted[520](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603212406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075943.htm) .


#### Warning letters: computerized system controls under 21 CFR 211.68(b)


These findings concern on-premise laboratory systems. They define the access, audit trail and backup controls inspectors expect from any GMP system, hosted or not.


Company (letter date) Finding


KVK-Tech (Feb. 11, 2020) QA staff had administrator access to chromatography software. Stand-alone instrument files could be overwritten without an audit trail record[324](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/kvk-tech-inc-592387-02112020) .

#### Form 483 observations


**Cloud and hosted systems.** Two observations name cloud hosting directly:


- **Seniorlife Technologies Inc (Feb. 20, 2026), Observation 4:** The firm could not show it had performed the review of the cloud provider's compliance certifications that its own quality agreement summary required for hosting of a production environment[358](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=358) .
- **S.M.A.I.O (Sept. 19, 2024):** The firm approved a risk analysis as complete even though a risk control was only partly implemented because the host vendor contract needed updating. The software uses cloud services to store patient data and images[359](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=359) .


A related web-application observation that does not turn on cloud hosting is Gobiquity, Inc. (Feb. 12, 2026): a CAPA on a web application release was not handled as a design change. The CAPA fixed the code but not the systemic change control failure or possible cybersecurity impact[510](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=510) .

#### What the enforcement record does and does not show


Searches of the FDA warning letter database for cloud, SaaS, web-based and third-party hosting terms did not identify a warning letter whose cited violation turns on the cloud hosting itself. Matches for "cloud" came from company names or contact details rather than findings[393](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/chuckin-clouds-vape-shop-inc-613515-02262021)[433](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/tasty-cloud-vape-co-llc-dba-tasty-cloud-vape-co-694342-10092024)[434](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/cloud-9-systems-llc-dba-cloud-9-vapor-565001-09212018) . The cloud-specific precedents found are Form 483 observations, and both concern supplier oversight and contracts rather than the technology[358](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=358)[359](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cloud-hosted-and-saas-gmp-computerized-systems?showSourceNumber=359) . The pattern in the letters is that FDA holds the firm accountable for validation and supplier qualification regardless of who performed the work[252](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/westwood-laboratories-llc-674728-04172024)[249](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423062156/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2014/ucm402449.htm)[251](https://web.archive.org/web/20151003020406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2012/ucm309306.htm) .
